topic_description: measuring media bias in language models for fairness in hate speech and misinformation detection

Bias-Aware Contrastive Learning.Problem: Current language models struggle to consistently detect and classify media bias across different demographic groups and topics, leading to unfair treatment in hate speech and misinformation detection.
Bias-Aware Contrastive Learning.Existing Methods: Existing methods often rely on supervised fine-tuning on labeled datasets or prompt engineering for zero-shot classification.
Bias-Aware Contrastive Learning.Motivation: Inspired by recent advances in contrastive learning and adversarial training, we propose a novel approach to make language models more robust and fair in detecting media bias.
Bias-Aware Contrastive Learning.Proposed Method: We introduce Bias-Aware Contrastive Learning (BACL), a two-stage training process. First, we generate a large corpus of synthetic biased and unbiased text pairs using a diverse set of demographic attributes and topics. We then train the model using a contrastive loss that encourages it to distinguish between biased and unbiased versions of the same content. To ensure fairness, we incorporate an adversarial component that penalizes the model for relying too heavily on specific demographic attributes when making bias predictions. This is achieved by training a separate adversarial classifier to predict the demographic attributes from the model's internal representations, and adding a gradient reversal layer to discourage the main model from learning these spurious correlations. Additionally, we introduce a novel 'bias swapping' data augmentation technique, where we automatically transform biased text to target different demographic groups, forcing the model to focus on the underlying bias rather than specific group associations.
Bias-Aware Contrastive Learning.Experiment Plan: We will evaluate BACL on existing media bias datasets such as MBIC and BABE, as well as on hate speech detection benchmarks like HateXplain. We will compare against state-of-the-art baselines including fine-tuned BERT and RoBERTa models, as well as few-shot prompting with large language models. To assess fairness, we will measure performance disparities across different demographic groups and topics. We will also conduct ablation studies to quantify the impact of each component of our method.

Dynamic Bias Calibration Network.Problem: Language models often exhibit inconsistent bias detection capabilities across different domains and struggle to adapt to evolving forms of media bias and misinformation.
Dynamic Bias Calibration Network.Existing Methods: Current approaches typically involve static fine-tuning or prompting strategies that may not generalize well to new domains or emerging bias patterns.
Dynamic Bias Calibration Network.Motivation: Drawing inspiration from meta-learning and dynamic neural networks, we propose a flexible architecture that can rapidly adapt to new bias detection scenarios and maintain consistent performance across diverse contexts.
Dynamic Bias Calibration Network.Proposed Method: We introduce the Dynamic Bias Calibration Network (DBCN), a novel architecture consisting of a base language model augmented with a set of lightweight, task-specific calibration modules. These modules are trained to recognize and adjust for different types of bias (e.g., political, racial, gender) and misinformation patterns. During inference, a meta-controller network dynamically selects and combines the most relevant calibration modules based on the input context. To train this system, we develop a multi-task curriculum that exposes the model to a wide range of bias scenarios. We also incorporate a continual learning mechanism that allows the model to efficiently update its calibration modules with new examples without catastrophic forgetting. Additionally, we propose a novel 'bias amplification' technique that artificially exaggerates biased language in the training data, making it easier for the model to learn to detect subtle forms of bias. To improve interpretability, we add an attention visualization layer that highlights the specific text segments and calibration modules most influential in the bias detection decision.
Dynamic Bias Calibration Network.Experiment Plan: We will evaluate DBCN on a diverse set of media bias and misinformation detection tasks, including news article bias classification, social media hate speech detection, and fake news identification. We will compare against static fine-tuned models, few-shot prompting approaches, and ensemble methods. To test adaptability, we will create a series of domain shift scenarios, introducing new topics and bias patterns not seen during training. We will measure both overall accuracy and consistency of performance across different domains and bias types. We will also conduct human evaluation studies to assess the usefulness of the model's interpretability features.
